meta.title: Skill book
meta.insideCover: Foundations first. Then frameworks. Then ship.
meta.leftLeafBody: Each turn is one tool I actually ship with — how I learned it, where I use it, and what I still watch for.
meta.introLede: Not a buzzword list. These are the tools I reach for when a product has to stay fast, accessible, and maintainable after launch day.
meta.introFooter: Next pages → each skill in depth

skills.name: HTML
skills.learned: I learned HTML the hard way — rebuilding client pages until headings, landmarks, and forms made sense to a screen reader, not just a designer. Real projects taught me that clean markup is the cheapest accessibility win.
practice: Landmark regions and heading order on every page
Forms with labels, errors, and keyboard paths

skills.name: CSS
skills.blurb: Layout, motion, and responsive design systems
skills.learned: CSS clicked when I stopped fighting it and started designing with constraints — grid, flex, container queries, and tokens. Most of my motion work is CSS-first so it stays cheap and theme-aware.
practice: Design tokens for color, type, and spacing

skills.name: Tailwind CSS
skills.blurb: Utility-first styling that ships production UI fast
skills.learned: I picked up Tailwind on shipping deadlines — then kept it because a shared utility language keeps design systems honest across pages. I still extract components when patterns repeat.
practice: Component extraction when utilities get noisy

skills.name: React
skills.learned: React became second nature through product UI — state that users can feel, forms that recover from errors, and components that stay readable six months later. I care more about composition than clever hooks.
practice: Composable UI with clear ownership of state

skills.name: Next.js
skills.blurb: App Router, SSR/SSG, and Core Web Vitals
skills.learned: Next.js is where my frontend and backend instincts meet. I learned it by shipping SEO-sensitive marketing sites and app shells that need fast first paint without giving up dynamic data.
practice: App Router routes with sensible caching
Image, font, and metadata tuning for CWV

skills.name: TypeScript
skills.blurb: Typed contracts that keep large apps maintainable
skills.learned: I adopted TypeScript gradually — first on API boundaries, then across UI props. It slowed me for a week and then saved me from an entire class of production bugs.
practice: Shared types between API and UI

skills.name: Laravel
skills.blurb: Secure APIs, queues, and domain-driven backends
skills.learned: Laravel is my default when a business needs auth, queues, invoices, or admin workflows yesterday. Years of client work taught me to design domains first, then controllers.
practice: Queues, jobs, and reliable side effects
Eloquent models that mirror the business

skills.name: PHP
skills.learned: PHP was my first serious backend language. Modern PHP (typed properties, attributes, Composer ecosystems) still powers a lot of the commerce and content work I ship.
practice: Clean service layers outside the framework glue
Secure handling of input and sessions

skills.name: Node.js
skills.learned: Node entered my stack for realtime features and JS-everywhere teams. I use it when streaming, sockets, or shared TypeScript models beat a split stack.
practice: Realtime channels where they earn their keep
Shared tooling with the frontend team

skills.name: Express
skills.blurb: Lean HTTP APIs with clear middleware layers
skills.learned: Express taught me to keep HTTP boring — routers, middleware, and explicit error paths. I reach for it when a focused API should stay small and readable.
practice: APIs that stay easy to document

skills.name: MongoDB
skills.blurb: Flexible document models with solid indexing
skills.learned: I learned MongoDB on product iterations that changed shape weekly. The skill is knowing when documents help — and when you need indexes and boundaries so flexibility does not become chaos.
practice: Schema design with real query patterns

skills.name: MySQL
skills.learned: MySQL is where I trust money, inventory, and permissions. I got good at it by debugging slow queries and designing schemas that still make sense after the feature set grows.
practice: Query plans before throwing hardware at it

skills.name: Redis
skills.blurb: Caching, sessions, and fast ephemeral state
skills.learned: Redis showed up whenever latency mattered — sessions, rate limits, cache keys. I treat it as a sharp tool: fast, intentional, and never the source of truth for critical data.

skills.name: Docker
skills.blurb: Reproducible environments from laptop to prod
skills.learned: Docker became essential once “works on my machine” stopped being funny. I use it so local, staging, and deploy targets share the same shape.
